correctness.rationale: One-point extension rank unrolls to a root with one full two-point profile in every relation state. Every relation-to-root class needs at least q+1 vertices. The support bound partitions root pairs from partner-class incidences: \(q^2-1\) root nonzero pairs, \(q^2(q-1)\) partner incidences, and at most \(\binom q2\) duplicate center-center pairs. The equality normal form meets all profiles with exactly \(q^3-\binom q2-1\) nonzero pairs. The \(q!/2\) assignments for each ordered cross-class pair, together with q-1 choices for each partner pair, prove the certificate-orbit count. A standalone checker verifies \(q=2,3,4,5\) constructions, all 5832 canonical \(q=3\) encodings, all 23 single-arc removals of one example, and every 6-vertex ordinary graph. No finite check is used to infer the all-q result.

value.rationale: The degree-3 extension condition is a natural finite threshold in an emerging Fraïssé-rank program. The theorem simultaneously determines minimal order and minimum interaction support for every free q-state pair signature, with a complete rigidity-based classification at the first boundary. In the natural oriented-graph case the exact 13-vertex / 23-arc threshold and the 5832 certified shapes measure a genuine jump from the known binary graph example. The general double-counting/equality method can be reused for other finite relational extension problems; the claim does not rely on an unsupported downstream application.
